quickstart.title: Quick Start
quickstart.subtitle: Run the full Inktide stack locally. Requires Docker, .NET 10 SDK, and Node.js 20+.
quickstart.step1Desc: Spin up Postgres, Keycloak, Redis, and MinIO with a single command.
quickstart.step2Desc: Create a .env file at the project root and fill in the required secrets.
quickstart.step3Desc: Build and start the .NET API host. All bounded context modules load automatically.
quickstart.step4Desc: Install dependencies and start the Next.js dev server.
quickstart.step5Desc: Start the embeddings and fact-extraction workers if you need RAG memory.

oauth.title: OAuth 2.0
oauth.subtitle: Inktide uses Keycloak as the identity provider. Third-party apps authenticate users via the standard Authorization Code flow with PKCE.
oauth.step1Desc: Go to Developer → Create App. You'll receive a client_id and client_secret.
oauth.step2Desc: Redirect the user to the Keycloak authorization URL with PKCE challenge.
oauth.step3Desc: POST the authorization code to the token endpoint to receive access + refresh tokens.
oauth.scopeChannelsRead: Read the list of connected channels for a soul
oauth.scopeMessagesReceive: Receive real-time message notifications via webhook
oauth.scopeSoulRead: Read public soul card info (name, avatar, description)

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.subtitle: Register a webhook URL in your app settings. Inktide POSTs a signed JSON payload to your endpoint on each event. Verify the signature before processing.
webhooks.step1Desc: Register an OAuth app at Developer → Create App and set a webhook URL + secret.
webhooks.step2Desc: Inktide POSTs JSON to your URL. Return HTTP 200 within 10 seconds.
webhooks.step3Desc: Check X-Inktide-Signature on each request to confirm authenticity.
webhooks.evMessage: A message was received and processed by a soul
webhooks.evResponse: The soul generated a response (text + audio ready)
webhooks.evConnected: A platform channel was linked to a soul
webhooks.evDisconnected: A platform channel was unlinked from a soul
webhooks.evTtsComplete: TTS synthesis finished; audio URL available in payload

realtime.title: Real-time (SignalR)
realtime.subtitle: Use SignalR to receive live audio, emotion, and viseme events as the AI soul speaks. The hub streams synthesized audio chunks immediately after TTS completes each sentence — latency from message received to first audio chunk is typically 500–1300 ms.
realtime.step1Desc: Exchange your Bearer token for a single-use WebSocket ticket.
realtime.step2Desc: Pass the ticket as the access_token query parameter.
realtime.step3Desc: Join a channel group to start receiving events for that soul.
realtime.step4Desc: The server pushes one event per synthesized audio segment.
realtime.tip1: SignalR WebSockets require a short-lived ws-ticket instead of a Bearer token in the
realtime.tip2: header. This is because browsers cannot set custom headers on WebSocket connections. The ticket is a single-use UUID stored in Redis with a 30-second TTL.
realtime.warn1: The ws-ticket is single-use and expires in 30 seconds. Do not cache it. If you use
realtime.warn2: , SignalR will re-use the same URL on reconnect — meaning the expired ticket will fail. Either disable auto-reconnect and handle it manually, or fetch a fresh ticket in the
realtime.mJoin: Subscribe to audio events for this channel
realtime.mLeave: Stop receiving events for this channel
realtime.lat3Val: Parallel with LLM tail — saves ~800 ms

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.subtitle: Polyglot monorepo — .NET 10 backend, Next.js 16 frontend, Rust media engine, Python AI workers. Latency budget: message received → voice in stream < 4 seconds.
architecture.pipelineSubtitle: From live chat to intelligent response
architecture.dependencyText: Dependencies always flow inward — outer layers depend on inner layers, never the reverse. Cross-context communication goes through APIs or Redis, never direct code references.
architecture.dependencyCaption: dependency flows left → right (outer depends on inner)

stage.chatSourcesDetail: Collects messages from multiple platforms in real time.
stage.connectorDetail: Ingests messages and publishes to synapse.ingest Redis Stream.
stage.synapseDetail: 7-stage scatter-gather — all stages run before LLM dispatch
stage.vllmDetail: OpenAI-compatible API — optimized for low latency (75% of latency budget)
stage.ttsDetail: Kokoro (default) — synthesis starts on the first LLM sentence, runs in parallel with generation tail.
stage.playbackDetail: Audio streamed via SignalR AudioHub → browser or OBS browser source.

lat.t1: Ingest, rate limit, context assembly (Redis + Qdrant + DB in parallel)
lat.t2: vLLM generation (75% of budget — GPU bottleneck)
lat.t3: TTS synthesis of first sentence (parallel with LLM tail)

ctx.organization: Multi-user org management — invites, memberships, roles
ctx.billing: Subscription management — Stripe + YooKassa webhook processors
ctx.graph: Visual node graph builder — node providers, handlers, graph execution engine
